claims.text: The provided WHO 2024 source does not contain a NICE-style 36-hour stopping pathway for early-onset sepsis. The available evidence focuses on the diagnostic accuracy of clinical algorithms and laboratory biomarkers rather than specific antibiotic discontinuation criteria based on culture timing.

The 7-sign IMCI algorithm for infants aged 0–6 days has good sensitivity and fair specificity when compared with physician judgement of sepsis. However, the source notes there was no evidence for culture-confirmed sepsis or mortality as the reference standard in this specific comparison.

Systematic reviews indicate that C-reactive protein (CRP) and procalcitonin (PCT) demonstrate good discriminatory ability to diagnose sepsis using blood culture as the reference standard in infants aged 0–59 days.
A 2019 systematic review of 20 studies involving 1615 infants reported that CRP had a sensitivity of 0.62 (95% CI: 0.50 to 0.73) at a median specificity of 0.74 for diagnosing sepsis in neonates.

For infants aged 0–59 days, the 7-sign IMCI algorithm shows fair sensitivity and fair specificity compared with physician judgement of sepsis, though no evidence was found using culture-confirmed sepsis or mortality as the reference standard.

The WHO 2024 source addresses diagnostic accuracy questions for young infants aged 0–59 days with possible serious bacterial infections, specifically in non-hospital settings, but does not provide explicit guidance on managing persistent clinical signs with negative cultures in a hospital setting.

evidence.text: 0–6 days: Good sensitivity and fair specificity ᵃ of the 7-sign IMCI algorithm compared with physician judgement of sepsis as the reference standard; there was no evidence for either culture- confirmed sepsis or mortality as the reference standard.

0–59 days and 7–59 days: Fair sensitivity and fair specificity ᵃ of the 7-sign IMCI algorithm compared with physician judgement of sepsis as the reference standard; there was no evidence for either culture-confirmed sepsis or mortality as the reference standard.

Two additional systematic reviews examined the diagnostic accuracy of laboratory biomarkers to diagnose culture-confirmed sepsis (88) or clinical or culture-confirmed sepsis (89) in infants aged 0–59 days at the time of presentation to health facilities. Brown et al.
